columns.name: acq_time
columns.description: The entry's instant in ISO-8601 with its UTC offset (e.g. ``2026-02-03T09:00:00+00:00``). The only timestamp a row carries, and BIDS' own name for it: ``pd.to_datetime(df.acq_time)`` reads it offset-aware in one step. Older files that split the instant across ``date``, ``time`` and a free-text ``timezone`` are read and folded into this column; only ``acq_time`` is ever written.

columns.name: is_final
columns.description: ``1`` on the configuration the patient was left on at the end of the visit, as marked by the clinician; ``0`` elsewhere. No row is ``1`` when the clinician did not mark one.

columns.name: is_starred
columns.description: ``1`` on a configuration the clinician starred during the visit as a particularly good one; ``0`` elsewhere. Any number of rows may be starred. A star records a clinical impression, not a ranking.

columns.name: program_id
columns.description: Stimulation program label (e.g., ``A``, ``B``).

columns.name: left_stim_freq
columns.description: Left stimulation frequency.

columns.name: left_anode
columns.description: Left anode contact(s) in the contact grammar: ``case`` for the can, ``E2`` for a ring, ``E2b`` for one segment, ``_`` joining several.

columns.name: left_cathode
columns.description: Left cathode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: left_amplitude
columns.description: Left amplitude in mA. A single value, or per-contact values joined by ``_`` in ``left_cathode`` order when current is steered (``3.3_2.2`` is 5.5 mA split 60/40). It carries no ``Units`` because a steered value is not a single number; sum the parts for the delivered current.

columns.name: left_pulse_width
columns.description: Left pulse width.

columns.name: right_stim_freq
columns.description: Right stimulation frequency.

columns.name: right_anode
columns.description: Right anode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: right_cathode
columns.description: Right cathode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: right_amplitude
columns.description: Right amplitude in mA, same shape as ``left_amplitude``.

columns.name: right_pulse_width
columns.description: Right pulse width.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text note recorded with this configuration.

scale_columns.description: One column per scale rated at this visit, placed before ``notes``: ``scale_`` plus the scale's name in lower case, every run of other characters turned into ``_`` (``Mood`` is ``scale_mood``, ``MDS-UPDRS 3.10 Gait`` is ``scale_mds_updrs_3_10_gait``); a second name giving the same column gains ``_2``. The cell is the rating alone, or ``n/a`` when the scale was not assessed. The sidecar gives each column's original scale name as its ``LongName``.

columns.name: acq_time
columns.description: The entry's instant in ISO-8601 with its UTC offset (e.g. ``2026-02-03T09:00:00+00:00``). The only timestamp a row carries, and BIDS' own name for it: ``pd.to_datetime(df.acq_time)`` reads it offset-aware in one step. Older files that split the instant across ``date``, ``time`` and a free-text ``timezone`` are read and folded into this column; only ``acq_time`` is ever written.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text note for this entry.

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: Session label as ``ses-<label>``: one row per visit of this participant.

columns.name: acq_time
columns.description: When the visit began, in ISO-8601 with its UTC offset: the start of its first run.

columns.name: target
columns.description: Anatomical target of the leads at this visit (e.g. ``STN``, ``GPi``, ``VIM``). Kept per visit, because a reimplantation can change it.

columns.name: left_electrode_model
columns.description: Left lead model at this visit, as named in ``schema/electrode_models.json``.

columns.name: right_electrode_model
columns.description: Right lead model, as named in ``schema/electrode_models.json``. The same as the left when both leads are the same model.

columns.name: left_ipg_model
columns.description: Implanted pulse generator driving the left lead at this visit, as named in ``schema/electrode_models.json`` or typed. Recorded only: the app does not change any setting from it.

columns.name: right_ipg_model
columns.description: Implanted pulse generator driving the right lead. The same as the left when one device drives both leads.

columns.name: filename
columns.description: The run's ``beh/`` file, relative to the session folder. One row per run, so each run of a visit keeps its own initial assessment.

columns.name: acq_time
columns.description: When the initial assessment of this run was annotated, in ISO-8601 with its UTC offset; the first configuration's time when there was none.

columns.name: medications
columns.description: Medications at this run, as noted in its initial assessment, free text.

columns.name: program_id
columns.description: Stimulation program the patient arrived on.

columns.name: left_stim_freq
columns.description: Left stimulation frequency.

columns.name: left_anode
columns.description: Left anode contact(s) in the contact grammar: ``case`` for the can, ``E2`` for a ring, ``E2b`` for one segment, ``_`` joining several.

columns.name: left_cathode
columns.description: Left cathode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: left_amplitude
columns.description: Left amplitude in mA. A single value, or per-contact values joined by ``_`` in ``left_cathode`` order when current is steered (``3.3_2.2`` is 5.5 mA split 60/40). It carries no ``Units`` because a steered value is not a single number; sum the parts for the delivered current.

columns.name: left_pulse_width
columns.description: Left pulse width.

columns.name: right_stim_freq
columns.description: Right stimulation frequency.

columns.name: right_anode
columns.description: Right anode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: right_cathode
columns.description: Right cathode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: right_amplitude
columns.description: Right amplitude in mA, same shape as ``left_amplitude``.

columns.name: right_pulse_width
columns.description: Right pulse width.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Notes of the initial assessment of this run.

scale_columns.description: The run's initial assessment: its clinical scales, named as in the session files' ``scale_<name>`` columns. The stimulation columns hold the settings the patient arrived on.

columns.name: participant_id
columns.description: Pseudonymous subject label typed by the clinician, as ``sub-<label>``.

columns.name: dbs_indication
columns.description: Condition the stimulation treats, from the app's list (``PD``, ``ET``, ``Dystonia``, ``OCD``, ``MDD``, ``TS``) or typed.

columns.name: participant_id
columns.description: Subject label as ``sub-<label>``, parsed from the source filename. The BIDS spelling and value shape deliberately, so this table joins directly onto ``participants.tsv``.

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: Session label as ``ses-<label>``, parsed from the source filename: the BIDS session, as ``sessions.tsv`` means it.

columns.name: run_id
columns.description: The BIDS run index, zero-padded, without the ``run-`` prefix so it sorts numerically.

columns.name: source_file
columns.description: The session or notes file this row came from. A notes file gives one row per note, with only ``acq_time`` and ``notes`` filled. Not redundant with the entities above: ``run`` defaults to ``01`` and does not auto-increment, so two visits on the same day can share all three, and this is then the only thing that tells their rows apart.

columns.name: is_initial
columns.description: ``1`` on the row of a visit's initial assessment, taken from its ``sessions.tsv`` row; ``0`` on a configuration tried during the visit.

aggregate_tsv.description: One row per configuration, and one per visit for its initial assessment: these identity columns, then ``dbs_indication`` and the visit's ``target``, lead and IPG models and ``medications``, then the session columns, with the union of every file's ``scale_<name>`` columns (``n/a`` where a file has no such scale).
